title: Client-side SDKs: latency-bounded workflows and graceful partial outputs (PRD draft)
body:
Summary:
This PRD proposes a small orthogonal surface on the Hosted API SDKs to make it easy for client apps to build latency-bounded workflows that rely on streaming, structured partial outputs, and tool-calls. Goal is to provide ergonomic primitives so SDK authors and app developers can express: (1) time-budgeted requests that accept partial results, (2) composable streaming events that include structured tool-handshake metadata, and (3) fail-open fallbacks (e.g., stop waiting and return best-effort partial state) with clear telemetry.

Why this is needed / problem statement:
- Many customers build real-time user experiences (chat widgets, coding assistants, search-with-chat) where 200–500ms perceived latency is a hard requirement. Blocking until a full generation (single non-streaming response) makes graceful UX impossible.
- We have several hosted streaming and tool-facing SDK features, but current ergonomics push complexity to customers: buffering transforms, heuristics to detect finality, stitching tool-call manifests into partial output.
- Without standard client-side patterns, teams re-implement brittle logic (timeouts, deduping events, merging partial JSON fragments) leading to bugs and inconsistent telemetry.

Goals (measurable):
- Provide SDK primitives so integrating apps can: request a time-bounded response and receive a deterministic partial payload if the model doesn't finish in time. (SLO: reduce customer-side custom code for partial outputs by 80% within 3 months of release.)
- Standardize a minimal event schema for streaming frames that carries typed chunks: text-delta, structured-token (JSON fragment), tool-invocation, tool-result, heartbeat, final-marker.
- Offer a high-level client API for "stream-with-time-budget" and "tool-handoff" that handles merging, backpressure, and optional application-level validation hooks.
- Surface telemetry: token-latency percentiles, partial-return rate, tool-invocation success/fallback rate.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not change server-side protocol (we use the existing streaming protocol and small header extensions).
- Not implementing a new serialization format — use JSON over existing frames.
- Not addressing batching/server-side autoscaling optimizations (server work tracked separately).

User scenarios / examples:
1) Chat widget with 400ms render budget
   - Widget calls SDK.streamWithBudget({model: 'rw-26b', budgetMs: 400, onFrame})
   - SDK returns incremental text frames; at 400ms it emits a 'budget-expired' partial payload containing the stitched text + best-effort structured fragments.
   - App renders partial reply and displays a subtle "Continue" affordance to fetch the full completion.

2) Assistant that needs to call an external tool
   - App sends prompt with desired tool-call permissions. Streaming frames include tool-invocation frames when the model suggests a call.
   - SDK halts main generation, emits tool-invocation event to the app which runs the tool and returns tool-result to the SDK. SDK resumes streaming, merging tool-result into structured output.

3) Mobile client over flaky network
   - SDK exposes small checkpoints (compressed) so partial results can be cached and shown immediately even when a full final marker is delayed.

Proposed API surface (high level) — keep minimal and idiomatic per language SDKs:
- streamWithBudget(opts)
  - opts: {model, input, budgetMs, structured: boolean (default true), onFrame(frame), validateFragment?: (fragment) => boolean}
  - returns: requestHandle with methods cancel(), extendBudget(addMs), awaitFinal()
- onFrame(frame) events:
  - frame.type in ["text-delta", "json-fragment", "tool-invocation", "tool-result", "heartbeat", "final", "budget-expired"]
  - frame.seq (monotonic id), frame.partial: boolean, frame.payload: string or JSON-fragment
- sendToolResult(requestId, toolResult)
  - when invoked, attaches toolResult to the open request context and resumes streaming.

Examples (pseudocode):
- JS snippet
  const req = sdk.streamWithBudget({model: 'rw-chat-v1', input: prompt, budgetMs: 350, onFrame: f => {
    if (f.type === 'text-delta') appendChars(f.payload)
    if (f.type === 'tool-invocation') callToolAndReturn(f.payload)
    if (f.type === 'budget-expired') showPartialStateAndEnableContinue()
  }})

- Short cURL example using existing HTTP streaming with header X-Client-Budget: 350
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Client-Budget: 350" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-chat-v1","input":"Summarize...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
  (SDK will translate header into hanging budget enforcement and emit budget-expired frame).

Streaming frame contract (minimal):
- All frames are JSON lines with fields {type, seq, ts, payload, partial} where payload is string or JSON (when type===json-fragment or tool-*).
- Final frame must be type==final with final: true and checksum of structured content (for integrity checks).
- Budget expiry is a deterministic server-side emission if the client provided X-Client-Budget header or SDK started a local timer; SDK must be able to emit budget-expired locally if connection stalls.

Client ergonomics notes / rules of thumb:
- SDK should enforce a sane default budgetMs (e.g., 400ms) for widget-level helpers but allow override.
- Provide glue helpers: stitchText(frames), reconstructJsonFragments(frames), validateAndMergeToolResults(toolResult, schema).
- Default behavior: when budget expires, SDK returns a stable, best-effort partial object that is parseable as the same structured type as final response (e.g., {content: "...partial text...", tools: [...partial-tool-states...]}) so apps don't need special parsing code.

Telemetry + observability (required):
- Emit events (per request) with tags: model, budgetMs, returnedType (final|partial|error|cancel), partialTokens, timeToFirstTokenMs, timeToBudgetExpireMs.
- Console UI: new per-route chart showing partial-return-rate and average partial completeness score (heuristic measured by fragment coverage).

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- Default SDK method names are additive; old code should continue to work. stream() remains available. New streamWithBudget is opt-in.
- Server will still emit existing streaming frames; SDK maps unknown frames into a generic "unknown" type and surfaces them so apps can opt-in to new frames.

Security & privacy:
- Tool-invocation frames must include a short permission token and minimal metadata (no credentials). Any tool-call that needs secrets must be executed on the app side.
- The SDK must not persist tool results to disk by default; provide explicit opt-in for local caching.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Prototype JS SDK helpers + examples (2 engineers, 3 weeks) — internal dogfooding in Console chat and Playground.
2) Built-in streaming contract on server side (small header support) + telemetry hooks (2 weeks).
3) SDKs for Python / Java / Go with identical semantics (4 weeks).
4) Beta with selected customers (4 weeks) — collect feedback on default budget, schema ergonomics.
5) GA and docs + migration guide (2 weeks).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should budget enforcement be purely client-side timer or require server acknowledgement? Hybrid model recommended, but need infra alignment (Linear RW-1347).
- How to best express resumable partial state for very large JSON outputs (streaming deeply nested JSON vs. chunked object model)? Propose chunked object model; need example formats.
- Compression of checkpoints for mobile caches — scope for later spike.

Implementation notes / infra dependencies:
- Server needs a small header handler for X-Client-Budget and to emit budget-expired frames if configured. This is low-risk and isolated.
- SDKs need deterministic merge helpers and extensive unit tests simulating partial ordering and reconnection.
- Console needs a new small panel for partial-return metrics and per-request event exploration.

Appendix: example frame sequence (simplified)
1 {"type":"text-delta","seq":1,"payload":"Hello, ","partial":true}
2 {"type":"text-delta","seq":2,"payload":"here's a quick","partial":true}
3 {"type":"tool-invocation","seq":3,"payload":{"tool":"search","query":"Redwood latency patterns"}}
4 {"type":"tool-result","seq":4,"payload":{"tool":"search","top":3,"items":[...]}}
5 {"type":"text-delta","seq":5,"payload":"...found some references.","partial":true}
6 {"type":"budget-expired","seq":6,"payload":{"reason":"client-timer"}}

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on API ergonomics and default budget. We want to avoid overly chatty frame types; keep primitive set small.
- Suggest any existing console metrics you'd like to see correlated with partial-return events.

Quick next steps:
- Product: finalize small API surface and default budget (this doc) — due 2025-12-17.
- Eng: prototype JS helper in playground branch and server header support — owner: Marcus Vale.
- Docs: write quickstart and migration guide once beta feedback is in.
